title: LLM Welcome Gate: staged conversion, validation, and profile publish pipeline
creator: Marina Cortez
description: Build a resilient, auditable end-to-end pipeline ("LLM Welcome Gate") that takes new open-source model weights from community submission through deterministic conversion, smoke validation, and automated performance profile publishing + pin recommendation. The goal is to reduce manual work for model engineers, shorten time-to-publish, and provide clear telemetry and rollback controls for risky variants. This ticket implements the orchestration, conversion worker contracts, validation suites, and the profile publisher integration into the catalog. It also defines human approval points and safety gates required by compliance.
background: Current intake process is semi-manual: engineers trigger conversions, run ad-hoc smoke suites, and manually create profile entries. This causes slow onboarding, inconsistent coverage across architectures (transformer variants, LoRA-adapted weights), and missing telemetry for early regressions. With increasing OSS model submissions we need a deterministic, observable pipeline that is safe for automatic pin suggestions and can gracefully hand off for manual review when risk thresholds are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: New model weights can be uploaded to staging with a signed manifest and metadata schema validated
Conversion service runs deterministically and emits a conversion artifact with checksum and runtime compatibility tags
Automated smoke validation passes for at least the baseline config (FP16 or quantized path) and emits latency/cost/quality metrics to the catalog
If smoke validation passes and risk thresholds are low, a draft performance profile is published to the catalog with a suggested pin; if not, the model is flagged for manual review
All pipeline steps produce audit logs and provenance links stored alongside the published profile
Ability to trigger a rollback/unpublish from the Console within 5 minutes of a failing rollout
Security review checklist completed for private builds and KMS usage logged
implementation_steps: Design manifest schema (weights, config, provenance, trusted-signer) and update intake API
Implement 'staging-orchestrator' job to fetch new submissions and create conversion tasks
Extend conversion-worker to support deterministic export modes and produce compatibility tags (seq-len, kv-cache layout, quant-mode)
Add a canonical smoke suite that runs sampling evals, latency runs, and token-accuracy checks; surface pass/fail and representative traces
Integrate telemetry publisher to send aggregated metrics to Console and model-catalog service
Add pin-recommendation microservice: consumes profile, applies heuristics (latency SLO, cost delta, quality delta) and emits suggested pin with confidence score
Create Console UI flow for manual approval, with diffs versus baseline models and one-click publish or send-back-to-engineering
Wire audit logging and signed manifests into the published profile record
Add automated rollback runner that can unpin and switch routes to fallback variants when a post-publish regression is detected
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Conversion non-determinism across GPUs. Mitigation: add deterministic flags and test matrix across vendor kernels; fail pipeline if mismatch detected
Risk: False-positive quality regressions from small eval sets. Mitigation: require multi-sample eval + heuristic smoothing and surface confidence bands
Risk: Latency metrics noisy during peak cluster usage. Mitigation: run dedicated smoke runners on isolated capacity or use percentiles over multiple runs
Risk: Sensitive customer weights leaking in logs. Mitigation: scrub manifests, encrypt payloads at rest with KMS, and restrict audit log access
decisions: Use signed manifests (ed25519) to assert provenance for community submissions
Default to publishing a DRAFT profile with suggested pin instead of auto-pinning unless confidence >= 0.9
Run quantized and FP16 conversion paths in parallel where possible to accelerate coverage
Telemetry schema will standardize on the model-catalog v2 contract (latency_ms_p50, cost_per_token_usd, top1_accuracy)
notes: We should coordinate with SRE to provision a small dedicated smoke pool for deterministic latency runs (requested in infra ticket)
Design wants a 'why-not-publish' explanation for failed auto-publishes to reduce back-and-forth with PMs
Expected data footprint per model conversion artifacts: ~1.5GB (converted weights) + 20MB metadata + traces
Consider adding a 'fast-path' for community models with existing verified manifests to skip manual step
